evidence: Workbook Quality Checks row 46 asks that the agent cannot read criteria or influence reward; quality-checks.md:184-185 requires no criteria, judge client, RewardKit or rubric in the agent image. Frozen task environment/Dockerfile:14-15 copies only instructions/ and assets/, creates an empty /app at :16-23, and never installs a judge or RewardKit. I read all six agent-facing notes and seed_data.json; none includes criterion text or grader machinery (a case-insensitive search for rubric/criteri/reward/score/judge/tests/logs/verifier/openrouter/api.key/claude/playwright/canary returned no matches). task.toml:2 exports only /app and /assets; :26-38 uses a separate verifier environment and puts the judge configuration under verifier.env. tests/Dockerfile:31 installs RewardKit and :43-44 copies tests privately to /tests then removes group/other access. test.sh:10-12 makes /logs/verifier mode 700 and /tests inaccessible to group/other; :104-111 launches submitted code as uid/gid 65534 under env -i with only PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT and DB_PATH; :207-227 runs RewardKit and score.py from /tests, with score.py:10 and :59-60 resolving private scoring.toml and writing /logs/verifier/reward.{json,txt}. The agent and verifier Dockerfiles and test.sh match the frozen template copies by SHA256. Adversarial source check: a broken app placing a fake tests tree or reward.txt under /app would not replace absolute /tests or root-owned /logs/verifier paths; a conforming app with different allowed UI/routes has the same isolation boundary. No container filesystem probe or full judge run was supplied for this row; this is a source-supported verdict, not runtime confirmation, and the raw-evidence-index.json was absent at review time.
